part: Melanges de Colbert 26, part I: diplomatic correspondence of Gaspard Coignet de La Thuillerie (French ambassador, mission to Denmark/Sweden 1644-1646, then back at The Hague 1646-1648) and Abel Servien (French plenipotentiary at the Westphalia congress, Munster/Deventer), 1644-1648
finding_aid: archivesetmanuscrits.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/cc955062 (FRBNFEAD000095506) -- lists 15 original La Thuillerie letters at fol. 1, 24, 27, 31, 35, 43, 50, 58 (La Haye, 1644-1648), fol. 11 (Hambourg, 1644), fol. 13 (Heiderslebe, 1644), fol. 15, 19, 21 (Coppenhaghen, 1644-1646), fol. 17 (Christianopoli, 1645), with Servien's response minutes at fol. 3 (Deventer), fol. 5, 8 (Munster); no mention of 'chiffre'/'dechiffre' anywhere in the finding-aid text. The starting-folio list for La Thuillerie's own letters (1,24,27,31,35,43,50,58) matches exactly the run of new-letter openings this leaf map found at canvas 4, 27, 30, 35, 39(->43), 47, 54, 62 (folio = canvas-3), confirming sender attribution at folios 27 and 31 that this map's eye-check subagent had marked uncertain.
folio_to_canvas: folio = canvas - 3, confirmed across the whole part (canvas 19 labelled '16' closes the Coppenhaghen 19 Nov 1644 letter fol.15-16; canvas 63 = folio 59, the last Part I leaf; canvas 64 = folio 60, Part II's own title leaf)

part_boundaries_corrected: Part I is NOT canvas ~4-69 as the prior KX-COLB26 boundary probe estimated -- this leaf map found Part I ends at canvas 63 (folio 59, last dated leaf 3 Feb 1648) and Part II's own title leaf ('Depesches de M. de Brienne, Tom.1er... Juillet-Decembre 1661') begins at canvas 64 (folio 60), with its table of contents at canvas 66-70 and its first actual despatch at canvas 72 (20 Juillet 1661, M. de la Meilleraye/Nantes). Canvas 65 duplicates canvas 64 (same title leaf, two capture files).
cipher_found: A large cluster, NOT limited to the one canvas-20 leaf flagged by KX-COLB26. Nomenclator-style numeral-group cipher (short 1-3 digit groups run inline with clear French, mixed with letters/symbols) appears on: canvas 20-21 (folio 17-18, La Thuillerie to Servien, dated 'A Christianopoli le 6 Avril 1645' -- see below for the contemporary decipherment gloss); canvas 26 (folio 23, dated '17e Mars 1646', salutation 'Mon Nepveu' -- NOT the usual La Thuillerie/Servien address form, possibly a different correspondent pair bound into the same volume, unresolved, a visibly larger/different cipher style, also carries some interlinear glosses); canvas 27 (folio 24, 1646, light cipher mixed into mostly plain prose); canvas 30-32 (folio 27-28, La Thuillerie to Servien, undated leaves, re Prince d'Orange); canvas 33 (folio 29, 1648, re payments); canvas 35-36 (folio 31-32, 1648); and a dense run through the whole final Jan-Feb 1648 stretch: canvas 39-40 (folio 35-36, closes 13 Jan 1648), canvas 47-51 (folio 43-47, closes 23 Jan 1648), canvas 54-56 (folio 50-52, closes 27 Jan 1648), canvas 62-63 (folio 58-59, closes 3 Feb 1648) -- i.e. essentially every La Thuillerie-to-Servien letter from Jan-Feb 1648 (the final weeks before the Munster/Dutch-Spanish peace) carries some cipher, typically a handful of numeral groups per page at the more sensitive points (Prince of Orange's politics, Spanish/Dutch treaty terms) rather than continuous encipherment. Several intervening canvases (28, 34, 37-38, 41-46, 52-53, 57-61) are plain prose (letters or continuations with no digits), so the cipher is used selectively, not as a running whole-letter cipher.
contemporary_decipherment_gloss: CONFIRMED on canvas 20-21 (folio 17-18) by this worker's own close-up crops (images/crops/canvas20_*.jpg): a smaller, different hand has written a plaintext gloss directly above or below specific numeral groups, e.g. 'Je parle des Suedois' over '6 25 zz 11 83 v 44 w\' 85', 'pour les Dannois qui' over 'Car 63 68', 'leur plaic[e]... ilz sont f[or]t abatuz' around '42 ilz estoient en 56 99'. This is a key-beside-the-letter case: a period decipherment written on the document itself, not yet transcribed into a key.tsv. The canvas-26 letter (folio 23, 'Mon Nepveu') also shows what look like similar small interlinear glosses (not closely verified). The Jan-Feb 1648 cipher runs (canvas 39-63) were eye-checked only at ~1000px by a subagent and NOT checked at high resolution for a similar gloss -- this is the single most important follow-up (a Christianopoli-style gloss on any of these leaves would hand a key straight over, exactly as at canvas 20-21).
